title: Add a gap-audit role that traces gaps to planning stages
summary: Add a new Athena role (modelled on the steward and audience roles) that reads logged gaps (interventions, introspections, rejections, independent ratings), traces each to the planning stage that missed it (reading, decomposition, assumptions, criteria, outcome check), and queues refinements to that stage's prompt or defaults. It also checks whether earlier refinements reduced later gaps of the same kind. Audience: the owner, who judges whether the next plan avoids repeat misses.

defaults_applied.how: The new module has unit tests and CLI tests; cargo test and clippy pass.
Tests feed sample gaps and assert the stage each is traced to and the refinement queued.
Zero gaps or an empty sample reports 'nothing to audit' or 'no evidence', not a reduction.
The stage set and effect check are enforced in code, not prose.
Reuse existing record readers, role, and work-queue machinery rather than new infrastructure.
One role, one command, no changes to the planning stages' own code beyond what refinements target.
Docs for the role are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The role is a new module in crates/athena-core, patterned on steward.rs and audience.rs, with a role definition in crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs (read at BRIEF.md line 533 and roles.rs).
Gap sources are the records already read by introspect.rs (interventions, introspections, rejections) plus audience ratings; no new record source is invented.

Stage attribution is a closed enum of five stages; a refinement is a queued work item or a proposal naming the stage prompt (e.g. crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md) as the target, respecting the ladder limits in roles.rs.
Effect check is computed by code: gaps of the same kind counted before and after the refinement landed, with an empty or too-small sample reported as 'no evidence' and not success.
Model calls go through the existing fake agent in tests; no live model is needed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a test gives the role gaps of each source kind (intervention, introspection, rejection, rating) and asserts each is traced to exactly one of the five stages: reading, decomposition, assumptions, criteria, outcome check.
Run cargo test: a test shows a traced gap queues a refinement work item that names the stage and cites the gap records, and a gap above the role's ladder limit becomes a proposal, not a change.

Run cargo test: a test shows the effect check reports 'reduced', 'not reduced', or 'no evidence' by comparing same-kind gap counts before and after a refinement; an empty sample never reports 'reduced'.
Run cargo test and cargo clippy: both pass with no warnings, and cargo fmt --check is clean.
The role has a recorded definition with a stable prompt, goal, cadence, and ladder limit, validated by RoleDefinition::validate, and a test asserts its path.
A docs page or a section in docs/design describes the role, the five stages, the gap sources, and the alternatives considered, so the owner can see how the next plan avoids a repeat miss.
The role can be invoked by a documented CLI command or cadence, and a CLI test using the fake agent exercises it end to end.

out_of_scope: Rewriting the planning stages' prompts beyond what tests need; the role queues refinements, it does not hand-edit every stage now.
The separate 'auditor and warden' addendum roles.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, or workflows.
departures: Larger than the reference: a new role spanning several crates, a CLI command, and a design doc, and the request is open-ended, so lower acceptance and pass odds and higher cost.
